text: The partner access record path is POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/partner-access-records on the rwb-decision base, with an Idempotency-Key, and answers 201 with entryId, chainSeq and entryHash or 200 with the first entry on a replay
why: No source names an operation for a partner access record: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 lists API-P7-001 to API-P7-008 and none of them, and Architecture v5 slide 14 names the ledger as an output only
read: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14; DP-13 base rule
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-access service owner confirm the path before the contract freeze
impact: The record path of the slice has no fixed address and the rwb-access call cannot be built or faked

text: The actions element of a partner access entry carries the partner firm reference, the partner role, the scope reference PLACED, the external gateway identity reference and the refusal reason code; inputs_ref carries the claim-set reference with matrix version PM-2026.11 and masking version MASK-SIT-01
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 declares actions and inputs_ref as jsonb and text containers without a composition, and no source gives one for this record
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-008, DF-DEC-014); legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 7 and 11
confirm: Solution architect and the data steward confirm the two containers
impact: The firm, the role, the scope and the identity reference have no agreed place on the entry and the two reads cannot filter by firm

text: final_call of a partner access entry carries the result as ALLOWED or REFUSED, held as a row of the service's own vocabulary beside LOV-DECISION
why: DF-DEC-012 final_call is required and no source names a value set for an access decision; the legacy story names the result as allowed or refused only
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-012); legacy RWB-E2-019 section 7
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-access service owner confirm the two values
impact: The entry either leaves a required column empty or carries an invented constant

text: The two decision-log reads are filtered by partnerId, decision, from, to, page and size, and the page-size bound is read as a parameter of rwb-case
why: TSD P7 v2 API-P7-006 names caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page and size for the general search and no source names a firm filter
read: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P7-006); DP-06; DP-07
confirm: Solution architect and the business analyst of P7 confirm the filter before the contract freeze
impact: The entries of a firm in a date range cannot be read and the page-size bound is missing

text: The claim-set reference of a record is an opaque string carrying the business date and the hash of the claim set with the matrix version and the masking version in force, and this service never resolves the claims
why: DF-DEC-008 inputs_ref is required and no source gives its shape for a partner access record; the seven field groups of FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-001-02 name an inputs reference only
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-008); FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-001-02
confirm: Solution architect and the security architect confirm the shape, which must carry no claim value
impact: The required column holds an invented value or the two versions are lost from the entry

text: A partner access record is appended on the record path within the resolution so a failed append refuses the access answer, and the same record is published on rwb.decision-record.v1 and deduplicated by the idempotency key so the ledger holds one entry; the five-minute collection stays the general ingest
why: The slice requires the fail-closed answer and Architecture v5 slide 28 collects the ledger within five minutes with strict mode only for points of no return; the two readings are reconciled by one record on two deliveries
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 28 and 42; legacy RWB-E2-019 section 5; R-UNI-39; DP-03
confirm: Solution architect, the rwb-access service owner and the Internal Audit representative confirm the reading before the contract freeze
impact: Either a session opens on an unwritten record or an entry exists for an answer that was never given

text: A partner access entry carries no case id: DF-DEC-002 case_id stays empty because the decision belongs to a firm and never to a case
why: DF-DEC-002 is optional in TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and the legacy story binds the partner session to a firm and a scope PLACED, not to a case
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-002); legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 9 and 11
confirm: Solution architect confirms that no case is written for a partner access record
impact: An invented case id would tie a firm-level access decision to a customer case

text: The database login of the service is the per-service rwb-decision login of DP-02; its name is not stated by any source and the story refers to it by the pattern only
why: DP-02 and Architecture v5 slide 29 fix one login per service without naming the identifiers
read: DP-02; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29
confirm: ACE team confirms the login name in the per-service DB story
impact: The story would name the shared monolith login or an invented one

text: The two index steps of the migration are ix_declog_partner_access on decision_code and decided_at and ix_declog_partner_firm_gin on actions, in V2026_2__decision_log_partner_access_index.sql
why: No source names the indexes that serve the firm and date-range search of the partner access entries
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1; DP-15 per-service Flyway sequence
confirm: ACE team and the solution architect confirm the index names and shapes with the query plan
impact: The firm and date-range read has no supporting index and the names are invented elsewhere

text: RW-AGENCYMG reads the entries of its own firm only and RW-AUDIT reads every firm with scope ALL, both decided by the authorise answer of rwb-access; the authorise contract is consumed and faked and is not in the C row of the story
why: TSD P7 v2 T6.1 gives R on the decision log to both roles and T6.2 states that scope filters every query, without naming the firm scope of a partner reader
read: TSD P7 v2 T6.1 and T6.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (POST /authorise)
confirm: Solution architect and the business owner of P7 confirm the firm scope of an agency manager
impact: The agency manager could read every firm, or an auditor could be refused a firm it must see

text: The shape of the D7.1 dispatch entry and of its two reads is read as follows and is written in the story as a placeholder, never as a guess: actions carries the notice reference and the notice type; outcome carries the hold reason or the delivery status, the notice period start date where the record carries one, and the message id the notice showed; finalCall is HELD, DELIVERED or UNSERVED as the legacy story writes the notice states; inputsRef is an opaque reference to the facts the conduct check read, with their freshness; the DecisionLogPage answer carries items, page, size and total and is filterable by caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from and to; and the dispatch record beside the notice is described without a panel id.
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 has no column for a notice, a notice type, a hold reason, a delivery status or a notice period start date, T-A.2 gives no answer field set and no notice-reference filter, and inventing any of them would put a value into the build that no owner approved.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1, T3.2, T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.4.2 AC-ALT-P7-001-02, A2.2.4.3 and A2.32.4.3; RWB-P6-E2021-CON events published; legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 4, 11 and 14; ownership.json api rows GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} to P7
confirm: Solution architect, with the data steward and the P6 business analyst, at the design review of wave 2 and in the OpenAPI of the service
impact: The entry, the two reads and the messages are built against the assumed shape; a later contract revision renames fields and messages without a change of behaviour, because the notice values themselves are rwb-comms's and are only referenced here

text: The rule version of a letter rule is the version of the rule package in force in the rule registry of this service, copied from the record as an opaque label of the shape the registry uses (the design gives package version labels such as ALLOC-2026.12) and validated by rule id and version against rule_row; the letter rules R-LIT-04, R-LIT-05, R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09 and R-UNI-20 are read as registry rows of that package; and a record with a rule id and no rule version is refused with MSG-P7-009 naming ruleVersion.
why: The legacy story and the P7 extracts require the rule id and version on every decision record, but no source writes the version label of the letter rules or says whether they are rule_row rows, and a composed label in code would be a business value in the wrong place.
read: FSD P7 v3 A2.3 and AC-EXC-P7-002-01; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 15 (rule_package_version and the version label shape) and slide 16 (rule_row read by rule ID and version; ruleId and ruleVersion in the decision record); TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-004 and DF-DEC-005; legacy RWB-E2-021 AC3 and AC6
confirm: Solution architect with the centre of excellence analyst and the rule custodian of rwb-decision at the rule-registry load of wave 2
impact: The label is copied, never composed, so a change of label shape or a move of the letter rules into another package changes a registry row and no code; until the registry rows exist the append refuses rather than writing a label it cannot verify

text: The six platform H dependencies, the one published C dependency and the two service baselines that the DP table adds are carried in the dependency map as DP-added rows and not in the metadata rows of the story, which keep Depends on (build) = None, Contract dependencies = RWB-P6-E2021-CON and Ready to start = Day 1; the reference-data reads of DP-07 stay inside the service at the version in force carried by the record until a later version calls the contract of rwb-case directly and adds its C row.
why: The metadata table of the work package fixes the two dependency rows character for character, and every added H is a platform CON story of wave 0 or 1 and every C is built against a published contract and its fake, so none of them blocks Day 1.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R5.7; the work package story line for RWB-P7-E2021-APP; TSD P7 v2 T3.1; the sibling P7 story RWB-P7-E2026-APP sections 3 and 13
confirm: Solution architect, dependency map owner, at the wave 2 build sequencing review
impact: Build sequencing keeps Day 1; the dependency map gains the rows the DP table requires, and no story in the lane waits on a platform contract

text: The capability area and the Decision log right of each operation are declared on the operation and enforced at gateway-bff through the composite route of DP-19, which asks the authorise answer of rwb-access; the caller's scope reaches the read as the declaration of the edge; this story adds no guard of its own and makes no authorise call, and it holds no role, scope or delegation row.
why: DP-08 is not in the pattern set that the work package fixes for this story, so an in-service guard would add a dependency and a behaviour that the story set does not declare; the refusal messages MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are the platform refusals of the authorise contract and are produced at the edge.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-08 and DP-19) and the work package pattern list; TSD P7 v2 T6.1 and T6.2; Architecture v5 slide 14; the sibling P6 story RWB-P6-E2021-APP section 10
confirm: Solution architect with the gateway-bff owner and the rwb-access team at the wave 2 access review
impact: A caller without the right is refused with 403 and a case outside the scope with 404; if the service must call authorise itself, one C row is added and the two reads keep their behaviour

text: MSG-P7-009 is the only message of this slice that a refused append produces, its text is carried as the placeholder 'Not specified in the source documents' until its owner publishes it, and the messages of the notice side quoted in the outcome of an entry (MSG-P6-008, MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-003 and MSG-P3-004) are copied unchanged from the legacy story and never rewritten here; the Thai text of every message follows decision DL10.
why: FSD P7 v3 names MSG-P7-009 in its exception flows and never writes its text, and the notice messages belong to rwb-comms and rwb-case, so writing either would invent a value or duplicate an owner's wording.
read: FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-002-01, AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05; legacy RWB-E2-021 section 14; RWB-P6-E2021-CON; decision DL10
confirm: Business analyst of P7 with the message catalogue owner of the platform at the wave 2 message review
impact: The refusal message and its Thai text change at the catalogue, not in the code; the four notice messages stay the owners' and are quoted only

text: The page-size bound of the search and the 5-minute completeness target of the ingest are parameters of the service read at the version in force, with no default held in code; a read that cannot obtain them refuses the page or the append rather than assuming a value, and their names follow the parameter naming of the service and are settled at the parameters load.
why: Architecture v5 slide 28 names the 5-minute completeness target as a value and no source names it as a parameter row, and a literal bound in the query controller would be a business value in code.
read: Architecture v5 slides 28 and 44; TSD P7 v2 T5.3 and T-A.2 API-P7-006; FSD P7 v3 A2.1 and A2.2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-06
confirm: Solution architect with the parameter catalogue owner at the parameters load of wave 2
impact: A threshold change is a parameter change and not a release; an unreadable parameter refuses the work instead of silently paging at a guessed bound

text: The shape of the contact entry and of its two reads is read as follows and is written in the story as a placeholder, never as a guess: the entry carries entryId, chainSeq, caseId, decisionCode, finalCall, ruleId, ruleVersion, inputsRef, an actions object holding the channel, the reason code and the requesting role, decidedAt, prevHash, entryHash, correctsEntryId and actorUserId, with no reason column of its own; the DecisionLogEntry answer carries the same fields and the DecisionLogPage answer carries items, page, size and total and is filterable by caseId with the from and to dates of TSD P7 v2 T-A.2; the inputs reference keeps the shape inputs/<businessDate>/<hash> of FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-001-02; and the search index of the case-and-date read is not named.
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 has no column for a channel, a reason code or a requesting role, T-A.2 names its answers without a field set, and inventing either would put a value into the build that no owner approved.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1 to T-A.2; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.4.2 AC-ALT-P7-001-02; legacy RWB-E2-022 sections 11 and 12; RWB-P6-E2022-CON section 12; the sibling P7 story RWB-P7-E2026-APP section 11
confirm: Solution architect, with the data steward and the P6 business analyst, at the design review of wave 2 and in the OpenAPI of the service
impact: The entry, the two reads and the index are built against the assumed shape; a later contract revision renames fields without a change of behaviour, because the contact values themselves are never held here

text: The refusal vocabulary of the contact check is read as follows: decision code X6 with final call contact refused covers all five causes of a refusal, and the cause is carried in the reason code as X6 Lost contact, X1 Dispute or complaint, No consent on the channel, Legal hold or Template withdrawn, the first two copied from the legacy message placeholder and the last three from the legacy scenario titles; the rule id of the entry is R-UNI-04 for a contact stop (with R-UNI-05 and R-DEV-16 as its supporting rules of BR2 and BR3, named in the rules rather than in rule_id), R-UNI-10 for no consent, R-UNI-20 for a legal hold and R-LIT-03 for a withdrawn template; a send that passed the check is appended with no reason code and with a final call that no source names, so the story carries it as a placeholder.
why: The legacy story names decision code X6 with final call contact refused only on the lost-contact refusal and names no decision value for the other four causes, P6 declares a record for every refusal and every send, and the reason-code labels and the rule id of a paired check have no source.
read: legacy RWB-E2-022 AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC11 and section 14; RWB-P6-E2022-APP section 12.3 and BR13; FSD P7 v3 A2.2; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and T3.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-04, R-UNI-05, R-UNI-10, R-UNI-20, R-DEV-16 and R-LIT-03
applied_in: RWB-P7-E2022-APP sections 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 (AC1 to AC6), 8 (BR1, BR2, BR7), 9 and 14
confirm: Business owner, with the solution architect and the Conduct and QA officer, at the design review of wave 2
impact: One code and one final call cover five causes and the cause is read from the reason code; if the business wants a code per cause, the reference rows change and the entries keep their shape with no code change

text: The rule version of an entry is the version the owning service returns with its answer, and the story names the label UNI-2026.11 for a universal rule because the P7 baseline carries it; the version label of R-LIT-03 is not fixed by any source and is carried as a placeholder rather than invented.
why: Architecture v5 slide 27 requires every answer to name the version used and the evaluation is embedded in the owning service, but no source gives a version label for the litigation rule set on this path.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 27 and 28; FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-001-02 (rule R-UNI-14, rule version UNI-2026.11); TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-005
confirm: Center of excellence analyst and the rule registry owner of rwb-decision, at the rule promotion of JOB-20 in wave 2
impact: The entry names a version in every case; only the label of R-LIT-03 changes when the litigation package version is published

text: The database login of the capability is the per-service login of DP-02 and the story calls it the rwb-decision login (DP-02); the right of the two reads is declared at gateway-bff because DP-08 is not in the pattern set of this legacy key, with a local guard that refuses closed; the page-size bound and the 5-minute completeness target are parameters whose names are not fixed; no feature switch of this story is named, the send switch rwb.comms.sms-line being P6's; and the message id set of this slice is the nine ids the legacy story and the P7 baseline carry.
why: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives every service its own login, no source fixes its name, DP-08 is absent from the pattern set of the key, and the parameter names, the switch and any further message id have no source.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 29, 41 and 45; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 rows DP-02, DP-08 and DP-11 and section R5.7; legacy RWB-E2-022 sections 12 and 14; TSD P7 v2 T6.2
confirm: ACE DB team at the schema and login allocation of wave 1, and the gateway-bff owner at the route review of wave 2
impact: One identifier in the migration and the deployment values, and one right declaration outside this service; nothing else in the story or its tests depends on them

text: The correction record and the send record are produced by rwb-document (P5) through the decision-record path of DP-03 inside the transaction of the action they record, and are appended to the ledger of rwb-decision in one atomic transaction of its own; a record that cannot be written stops the action with MSG-P7-003, so a refused signature start leaves no SENT_FOR_SIGNATURE entry.
why: Architecture v5 slide 28 moves the record to the local library with a central collection inside a completeness window, while legacy RWB-E2-017 AC9 and BR9 require the action itself to fail when the entry cannot be written; the two readings are joined so that no action proceeds unlogged and no record exists for an action that was refused.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-017 section 4 steps 6 and 9, section 5 X6, AC9 and BR9; Architecture v5 slide 28; Temporal and Drools design slide 14 (RecordAndApply)
confirm: Solution architect and Risk
impact: If the order is read the other way, a refused send would leave the SENT_FOR_SIGNATURE entry and the retry would need a duplicate rule instead of a rollback; the document states and the incident path do not change.

text: The payload of the two records, the final call of the correction entry, the shapes of the document set reference and of the write-once reference and the value pair identifiers are read from the published RWB-P5-E2017-CON declaration and the reference lists in force; no literal is written and no shape is assumed by this service.
why: The legacy story names the values and the decision code but not the record payload; the record container is TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and the content of actions, outcome and inputs_ref is not specified anywhere.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-017 AC2, AC3 and section 12; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and T-A.1; FSD P7 v3 A2.4
confirm: Solution architect
impact: A different payload from the P5 contract needs a mapping change in DecisionLogAppendService and no change to the scenarios apart from the field names.

text: The page-size bound of the search and the completeness target of the ingest are parameters of DP-06 with no name in the sources; the story holds no default and refuses the read or the append rather than assuming a value.
why: The parameters exist in the target (FSD P7 v3 A1.4 and the page shape of the reads) but the sources name no parameter code for either.
read: FSD P7 v3 A1.4 and A2.1; TSD P7 v2 T-A.1; Architecture v5 slide 28
confirm: Solution architect and Business analyst
impact: If the parameters are not loaded, both reads and the append are refused rather than served on a default; no business rule changes.

text: The message ids of this slice are the legacy ones and a duplicate record is refused with MSG-GEN-004; no new message id is introduced, and the text of MSG-P4-003 is left to its owner.
why: Legacy RWB-E2-017 section 14 gives the texts of the other messages and names MSG-P4-003 only in the error mapping of its section 12.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 12 and 14; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.4
confirm: Business analyst
impact: A new message id, if the P5 contract adds one, extends the table of section 14 without changing a rule.

text: No feature switch of this story's own is named by a source; the capability is present wherever a record arrives, and the switch rwb.document.generation-screens of the legacy story names the screens only and belongs to rwb-document.
why: Legacy RWB-E2-017 section 13 defines the switch for the screens and the send step, not for the ledger side.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-017 section 13; RWB-P5-E2017-CON
confirm: Tech lead
impact: A switch on the ledger side would hide the reads and the append; the record path of the producer already gates the capability.

text: The decision-log store baseline of rwb-decision (decision_log_entry with the columns of TSD P7 v2 T3.1, tr_declog_append_only, the missing UPDATE and DELETE grant, and the chain check JOB-14 at 02:00) and the authorise answer of rwb-access are the service's existing baseline and sit in no H or C row of this story.
why: The metadata rows of the WP give H None and C RWB-P5-E2017-CON, while DP-03 and DP-11 add the platform contracts and the authorise call; the baseline itself is earlier P7 work.
read: WP B-P7-02 story line for RWB-P7-E2017-APP; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and T6.1; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 44
confirm: Tech lead
impact: If the baseline is not in place, the story waits on the P7 decision-log store story and its own dbDelta rather than on a contract; the scenarios do not change.

text: The per-service login of rwb-decision has no name in any source. This story refers to it as the rwb-decision login (DP-02) and never to the monolith login.

confirm: The ACE DB owner who creates the schema and the login (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB)

confirm: The rwb-decision tech lead at merge

confirm: The rwb-decision tech lead and the plan check owner

confirm: The solution architect and the data owners of rwb_case and rwb_access

confirm: RWB-P1-E1001-APP as the owner of the dictionary

confirm: The rwb-decision tech lead
impact: The story starts on Day 1 against the service baseline and its fakes; no lane depth and no build order changes.

confirm: The solution architect who owns the LDM
